memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Do not eat any detestable thing. These are the animals you may eat: the ox, the sheep, the goat, the deer, the gazelle, the roe deer, the wild goat, the ibex, the antelope and the mountain sheep. You may eat any animal that has a divided hoof and that chews the cud. However, of those that chew the cud or that have a divided hoof you may not eat the camel, the rabbit or the hyrax. Although they chew the cud, they do not have a divided hoof; they are ceremonially unclean for you. - Deut 14:3-7 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Here begin the well-known food laws, distinguishing clean animals Israel could eat from unclean ones they could not. These rules touched the most ordinary part of daily life — what was on the dinner table. Every meal became a reminder that Israel belonged to God and was called to be different from the nations around them. Their holiness was not confined to the temple; it reached into the kitchen, into the everyday choices of life.

It is important to understand what "unclean" means here. It is a ceremonial category, not a moral one. An unclean animal was not sinful or evil; it was simply set outside the boundary God drew for His people's diet, to mark them as distinct. These laws served to teach Israel that they were a set-apart people, and that their God cared about every corner of their lives, even their food.

For believers today, these food laws are no longer binding. Jesus declared all foods clean (Mark 7:19), and the New Testament makes clear we are not to be judged over what we eat (Col 2:16-17; Rom 14:17). We are free. But the deeper principle endures beautifully: holiness reaches into ordinary life. Our devotion to God is not just for Sundays or spiritual moments; it touches how we eat, work, speak, and spend our days. "Whether you eat or drink or whatever you do, do it all for the glory of God" (1 Cor 10:31). You belong to God in the everyday. Let that shape even your smallest choices today.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Does my devotion to God reach into ordinary, everyday choices?
- Do I understand "unclean" here as ceremonial, not moral?
- How can I live for God's glory in the small routines of my day?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, thank You that I belong to You not just in spiritual moments but in the ordinary routines of life. Thank You for the freedom I have in Christ. Help me to live for Your glory in everything — even my smallest, most everyday choices. Amen.
